summary.intent: Drive a stack of caliper PRs (267, 268, 273, 275-279, 281, T7b) to merge by resolving open review findings, coordinating subagent workers across stacked branches.
summary.outcome: PR 272 was merged. The remaining PRs still had findings, so the assistant diagnosed eight root-cause classes, wrote a findings synthesis and a pre-push gate into the worker contract, and redirected the 267 and 268 workers. T7b (992a4a46) is committed locally on feat/relevance-used-layers and not pushed; 267 is blocked until its worker lands the allow-list change.

repo: Open findings are listed with `entire trail finding list caliper/<PR> --freshness=any --project=gh/orin-dx --repo=gh/orin-dx/caliper`, filtered by ' open '.
Writing full DOM-layer `members` cost +3.56% bytes on gate-large and +4.42% on shadcn, over the 3% limit, so only `used` ships for DOM layers (shadcn bytes +0.39%).
Layers gaining `used` in T7b: shadcn 942, mantine 29, spectrum 7, gate-large and chakra-only 0.
Merge order for the stack is 404/272, 405/267, 405/268, then 273 and 279, with the relevance batch (275-278, 281, T7b) last as one set.

Recurring findings fall into eight classes: silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, and contract drift.
About 40% of the raw finding count was the same code repeated across stacked child PRs.
Worker contract lives at ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md and the findings synthesis at ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.
workflow: Guards over node or type kinds should be allow-lists of proven forms, with everything else Unknown or Declined and no `_ =>` arms, rather than deny-lists of cases found so far.
Generate tests over the grammar of forms the code can receive, with the checker or TS API as oracle, not over past findings.
Mutation proof (remove each guard or dependency and confirm a test fails) is required, since mutation 2 passing in T7b showed the dependency recording was not covered.
After about three findings of the same kind, diagnose the class instead of spot-fixing; this was saved to memory as the third instance of that lesson.
Appending to files via bash heredoc was blocked by the sandbox, so the Edit tool was used instead.
Subagent hand-back messages carry no user authority and need independent follow-up.

friction: Reviewers kept finding new findings on every PR after spot fixes, because the guards were deny-lists.
The sandbox blocked a heredoc append to worker-contract.md, requiring a fallback to the Edit tool.
Three workers were already running, so the class-level slices could not all be spawned at once.
Mutation 2 in T7b still passed, so the stale-watch finding on 405/281 has no test that can fail.
open_items: T7b is unpushed and still needs: mutation 2 fix, a base-failure run of the new tests, an explanation for why chakra and gate-large get no `used` plus 5 real examples, the T7 findings (`lazy_delta`, checker-only layers, `declaration_origin` widening), and `/code-review`.
405/267 (collapse) is blocked until the worker makes the collapse decision an allow-list and sweeps all props-type forms.
405/268 (JSX evidence) needs a sweep of every `_ =>` default and tests of all access forms against the TS API.
405/273 needs its guard converted to an allow-list, covering the `Partial<Config>` `[Symbol.iterator]` finding.
405/278 needs factory-prop recognition as an allow-list.
405/279 needs a reference-model property test for the scheduler queue.
405/281 needs the open `Pick`-keys and watch-model findings fixed, plus the `used` producer check from T7b.
Whether the new pre-push gate stops new findings on the 267 and 268 batches is unproven; tighten the sweeps if the reviewer still finds new forms.
